quotes.text: Meduza also recorded serious rockabilly songs with a distinct 1950s flavour in his own studio, called Studio Ronka. He played most of the instruments himself.

One of Meduza's personas was the vulgar E. Hitler. In this guise he generally recorded more offbeat recordings like "E.Hitler skiter" (a recording of his own defecation) and sexually explicit material.

Many of Meduza's songs are about alcohol, women, and cars, often with obscene lyrics. Some songs are politically oriented, with many aimed against the various Swedish governments in power during his musical career.
His songs contained lyrics about cars, girls, and alcohol and were laced with obscenities. He also tackled politics and spoke out against the Swedish government.
Eddie Meduza also recorded more eccentric material under the pseudonym E Hitler, playing raggarmusic, which was a dirtier, greasier form of rockabilly.
His recordings under the name Eddie Meduza were deeply influenced by raw and rare 1950s rock and roll, hillbilly, and rockabilly records.
On most of his recordings, he handled all the instruments himself, which made has albums sound even more primitive.
A controversial live artist, Eddie Meduza was known for his alcohol-driven confrontational performances.
